metadata.title: English Crossword Puzzles by CEFR Level
metadata.description: 61 themed crossword puzzles (10 per level, 11 at A2). Themes, word length, word frequency and clue complexity are calibrated to each CEFR level. Answers may contain spaces or hyphens; the grid uses letters only and the clue shows the word lengths.
metadata.framework: CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages)

To use deliberately ambiguous language so as to avoid committing oneself.
To acknowledge, often reluctantly, that an opponent's point is valid.
A counter-argument intended to refute a claim.
A distorted version of an opposing position, set up only to be knocked down.
Deliberate exaggeration for emphasis or effect.
Needless repetition of the same idea in different words, as in "free gift".
A mild or indirect expression used in place of one considered too blunt.
To confirm or lend support to a claim with additional evidence.
Superficially clever but deceptive reasoning.
Directed against the person rather than the position they maintain.
A division into two sharply contrasted or mutually exclusive categories.

puzzles.description: Schools of thought and moral theory.

words.clue: Holding that the right action is whichever produces the greatest good for the greatest number.
The rejection of all moral principles, often in the conviction that life is meaningless.
The branch of philosophy concerned with the nature, scope and limits of knowledge.
The doctrine that every event, including human choice, is the inevitable result of prior causes.
Disinterested and selfless concern for the wellbeing of others.
Concerned with individual freedom, choice and the search for meaning in an indifferent universe.
The view that the self is the only thing that can be known to be real.
Inclined to lay down principles as undeniably true, without regard for evidence.
The position that truth and morality are not absolute but contingent on culture or context.
Inquiry into the fundamental nature of reality, being and causation.
Kant's ___ imperative: a moral obligation that holds unconditionally.
An ancient school advocating the calm, rational endurance of what cannot be changed.

puzzles.description: Nuanced adjectives of personality.

words.clue: Excessively eager to please or obey; fawning.
Generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful.
Making a show of being morally superior to others.
Bad-tempered, argumentative and uncooperative.
Fond of company; sociable.
Showing a lack of courage or resolve; timid.
Not showing proper respect; cheeky.
Very attentive to accuracy and detail; exacting and hard to please.
Modest or shy owing to a lack of self-confidence.
Having an unemotional, stolidly calm disposition.
Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior.
Persisting tirelessly; incapable of being worn out.

puzzles.description: Honesty, lies and manipulation.

words.clue: Not candid or sincere, typically by pretending to know less than one does.
Given to telling lies.
Deceitful double-dealing.
To render deliberately obscure or unintelligible.
Conformity to facts; truthfulness.
A trick or stratagem used to evade a rule or conceal a purpose.
A person falsely claiming special knowledge or skill; a fraud.
Manipulating someone psychologically into doubting their own memory or perception.
To invent false information in order to deceive.
To conceal one's true motives, feelings or beliefs.
Having an excessive readiness to believe things.
Plausible on the surface but false; not genuine.

puzzles.description: Hierarchy, authority and social control.

words.clue: Dominance of one state or social group over others, often maintained through consent.
Government by a small, privileged group.
To deprive someone of the right to vote.
The practice among those in power of favoring relatives, especially in appointments.
A system in which advancement is based on individual ability and achievement.
A leader who gains support by exploiting popular prejudices rather than rational argument.
To bring under domination or control, especially by conquest.
To accept something reluctantly but without protest.
The transformation of a working-class neighborhood by affluent newcomers, often displacing existing residents.
A person who openly opposes official policy, especially in an authoritarian state.
A person or group made to bear the blame for the failings of others.
A violent uprising against an established authority.

puzzles.description: Elevated words for refined expression.

words.clue: Lasting for a very short time.
Seemingly present everywhere at once.
Carried out with minimal effort or reflection, merely as a routine duty.
Representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class.
The occurrence of fortunate discoveries by chance.
Sweet and smooth; pleasing to the ear.
Too great or extreme to be expressed in words.
To place side by side, especially for contrasting effect.
Looking or sounding mournful and dismal.
To make a problem, bad situation or negative feeling worse.
To drain of energy or vitality; to weaken.
So intense as to seem almost tangible.

puzzles.description: Words to describe how people speak and write.

words.clue: Using more words than necessary.
Using very few words, sometimes to the point of seeming rude.
Brief but full of meaning.
Pompous or extravagant in language, especially to impress.
The everyday language spoken by ordinary people in a region.
A grammatical mistake or a breach of good manners.
The comic misuse of a word in place of a similar-sounding one.
A pleasing quality in the sound of words.
Tediously lengthy in speech or writing.
A remark used too often to be interesting or thoughtful.
A newly coined word or expression.
The use of many words where fewer would do, often to be evasive.

puzzles.description: Fine shades of feeling, from gloom to elation.

words.clue: A deep, lasting and often thoughtful sadness.
An intense feeling of excitement and happiness.
Listless weariness arising from a lack of interest or occupation.
Annoyance or distress at having failed or been humiliated.
Bitter, long-lasting resentment.
Full of vague or regretful longing.
In low spirits from loss of hope or courage.
Ecstatically happy, often after a success.
Feeling or expressing sincere remorse.
Anxious that something bad will happen.
Angry at what is perceived as unfair treatment.
Pitifully sad and lonely.

puzzles.description: Abundance, scarcity and attitudes to money.

words.clue: Having little or no money.
Having a great deal of money; wealthy.
Extremely unwilling to spend money.
Recklessly extravagant or wasteful with resources.
Without the basic necessities of life.
Generosity in giving money or gifts.
Ostentatiously rich and luxurious.
Sparing or economical with money or food.
The practice of donating money to good causes.
Poor and needy (formal).
Extreme greed for wealth.
To waste money or an opportunity recklessly.

puzzles.description: Hostility, deadlock and making peace.

words.clue: Strong hostility between people or groups.
Hostile and aggressive, eager to fight.
Intended to placate or pacify.
The re-establishment of friendly relations, especially between states.
Bitterness or ill feeling in speech or manner.
A situation in which no progress is possible; a deadlock.
To pacify by giving in to demands.
An agreement to stop fighting for a certain time.
Refusing to change one's views or to agree.
To calm someone's anger or anxiety.
A noisy disturbance or quarrel.
The easing of hostility between countries.
